title: Balfour to Cornwallis (March 1781) and Balfour to Stewart (12 Aug 1781), cipher letters intercepted by the Americans (NARA RG 360, PCC item 51 vol. 1, pp. 717-736)

steps.what: NARA proxy API for PCC item 51 vols. 1-2: Fold3 image descriptions filtered for cipher/Cornwallis/Balfour; candidate images downloaded.

Saberton JAR 2019 (Common cipher: ring, number for A first, fillers from 30; no evidence the Americans broke it); NSA history and Washington to Lovell 6 Oct 1781 (Lovell broke the Clinton/Cornwallis cipher). Cornwallis Papers 2010 not checked.
p. 717 by hand against the interlinear: numbers below 50 letters, 50 and over fillers; 'the principal occurrences since you left us'.
Two agents transcribed pp. 717-725 (numbers, interlinear, notes), 168 lines.
key_from_interlinear.py: one fixed number-to-letter table per sheet, by edit-distance alignment with the interlinear: 20-27% agreement.
ring.py: Saberton's ring with a setting per dash group, 26 letters: long runs read, i/j and h/i confusions.
25-letter alphabet (i = j): one ring order of 25 numbers fits all pages.
Braced groups (fillers plus one number) are setting indicators, the number = A; decode.py deciphers No. 1 from the ciphertext alone.
p. 718 indicator gives a=25; the decipherer wrote 'should be 13'; a=13 reads 'two troops under Colonel Fenwick'.
Indicators with two fillers decided by en-modern on the next 40 letters; indicator groups split at line ends; two fillers cut at the page edge marked 4x.
Nos. 2 and 3 open without indicator: No. 2's first six numbers read 'bridge' under No. 1's last setting; all 25 settings scored for No. 3, a=14 (No. 2's last) reads. Settings carry across sheets.
Lone numbers between dashes are numerals in clear (82, 84, 71, 64, dates, 18 men and 40 horses), except a lone number reading 'a'.
Agent transcribed pp. 729-736 (letter B and the Stewart letter).
Ring and indicator rule applied unchanged to B: 99.4% of letters in English windows.
Ring on the Stewart letter (C): all 25 settings fail (per-char -6.9 to -10.4).
C's interlinear aligned with fillers >= 40 removed: a fixed table of 21 values (5-99 votes each); k=34 and e=1 from context. C deciphers 100% in English windows; 2, 3, 19, 30 open.
Same window measure on Nos. 1-3 deciphered with a corrupted ring (neighbour swaps): 2.1%, 0.0%, 0.0%.
reading.md and decoded.txt (cipher, interlinear and decipherment per line) written.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 6151 tokens, 533 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.241 per letter; random keys -7.258 (z 23.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -4.101 (mean -4.156, z 37.9); annealer on the real text -3.66. Verdict: pass.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) reading only RING and TABLES['C'] of decode.py and the transcription pages, with dash-group rules and no language model: A 2742/2742, B 1539/1539, C 850/850 letters equal to decryption_A/B/C.txt; the same 31 + 4 indicator settings, and Nos. 2 and 3 open on the previous sheet's last setting without the START table. README read bar (v10_relabel.measure): A 0.988, B 0.990, C 0.970 (recorded 1.0, 0.994, 1.0); all stay read. Image p. 725 (NARA image 570): over 15 in L09 the interlinear has an f (15 = the f of 'of'), and the word over the numeral 18, read 'fifteen', is faint and partly struck through, ending '-teen'; the cipher's 18 stands.

Project check of PR #572 (Brice Dudout): his decoder re-run (A 2742/2742, B 1539/1539, C 850/850 letters, 31 + 4 indicator settings); v10_relabel.measure reproduced (A 0.988, B 0.990, C 0.970) and recorded as read_share in place of 1.0, 0.994, 1.0, which were letter shares; all stay read. p. 725 L09 looked at on NARA image 570: the mark over 15 looks like an f, the struck word over 18 is too faint to decide between fifteen and eighteen; the cipher's 18 stands. No key correction.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.239; polyphony 0.0; 198 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.66

outcome.method_basis: Every cipher page carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment (probably Lovell's, 1781); the ring key and setting rule were rebuilt from it and the letters deciphered from the transcribed numbers alone, which agrees with the interlinear and corrects its faint or slipped letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py: letters in 24-letter windows scoring >= -3.3 per char on lang en-modern (A 2742/2742, B 1530/1539, C 850/850); control with a corrupted ring 0-2%.

credits.note: interlinear decipherments in PCC item 51 vol. 1, pp. 717-736, probably James Lovell, 1781
independent decoder without language model (100% of A, B, C), README read-bar recount, p. 725 checked on the NARA image

gaps.item: A, B: 12 illegible tokens at page edges and blots

outcome.notes: Nos. 1-3 are one dispatch; the setting carries across sheets. C is a different cipher. The Cornwallis/Wemyss/Craig cipher passages in the same volume (translations pp. 759-761) were not transcribed.

texts.label: A. Balfour to Cornwallis, Nos. 1-3, March 1781 (pp. 717-725)
texts.summary: Charleston news for Cornwallis after he left: the Chatham convoy with Governor Bull and Sir Egerton Leigh, the raid of Marion and Lee on Monk's Corner, Craig's seizure of Wilmington, Georgetown attacked, a fleet from Ireland, Arnold's express from the Chesapeake, Captain Barclay refusing to sail against the French, and Sumter beaten off at the Congarees and pursued by Rawdon and Watson.

reading_review.note: Read through in full against decryption_A.txt: continuous military news in plain sentences, every proper name historically placed (Bull, Egerton Leigh, Monk's Corner, Fenwick, Wilmington 28 Jan, Barclay's ships, Sumter at the Congarees 19 Feb). The shape score (0.655) is pulled down by the long semicolon-joined sentences of the original and the [?] at two word gaps, not by unread text. Not checked by a human against the images.

texts.label: B. Balfour to Cornwallis, about March 1781 (pp. 729-732)
texts.summary: Arnold's plan to raid the Albemarle Sound and Newbern; Balfour has sent Arnold the cipher by Evans; Savannah short of provisions, the frontier under pressure; what to do with the troops from England and the Wilmington post; Rodney's capture of St Eustatius and a Dutch war certain.

reading_review.note: Read through in full: Arnold's paragraph, the cipher sent by Evans, Savannah, Wilmington, Rodney at St Eustatius; one place of a phrase ('By the bearer') uncertain. Not checked by a human against the images.

texts.label: C. Balfour to Lt Col. Alexander Stewart, 12 Aug 1781 (pp. 733-736), cipher runs
texts.summary: Arrangements for an escort and supplies to Stewart's army: no dragoons at Charleston, the depot near Monk's Corner put in defence, Caldwell not to act with the cavalry, and a request to cover the escort at Manigault's or Murray's ferries with a move towards Nelson's.

reading_review.note: Cipher runs only, each read as sense; the clear text between them is not edited here, so the runs are fragments of sentences; 'Tuesday', 'rent' and 'the next' grade C. Not checked by a human against the images.
